title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: AMODEI PUBLISHES "WE MUST PACE THE FRONTIER" (12 SEP) — ANTHROPIC UNILATERALLY COMMITS TO EMBEDDED THIRD-PARTY EVALUATORS WITH EMPLOYEE-LEVEL ACCESS AND PUBLISH RIGHTS, AND ALTMAN COMMITS OPENAI TO THE SAME WITHIN 48 HOURS
bullets.summary: Read in full at the primary (darioamodei.com, dated September 2026). A three-step plan: (1) EMBEDDED EVALUATORS — outside teams such as METR get desks in Anthropic offices, access badges, company laptops and permissions "mostly comparable to what internal risk assessment teams have," plus a contract giving them the right to publish findings about risk levels, incidents, practices and the access they did or did not receive, without Anthropic's editorial control; redaction is limited to security-sensitive, legally privileged, commercially sensitive or third-party confidential material, and explicitly cannot remove findings "just because they are unfavorable," with reviewers free to say publicly that a redaction removed something material. Anthropic is committing to this UNILATERALLY and now. (2) DEMOCRATIC COORDINATION on common safety standards and limits on the rate of unchecked progress, with government mediation or antitrust waivers. (3) GLOBAL COORDINATION across four escalating levels, from banning narrow dangerous uses up to a speed limit on recursive self-improvement, which Amodei calls "difficult but just on the edge of being possible." Two stated causes: RSI accelerating industry-wide "since roughly this summer," and the OpenAI–Hugging Face agent-swarm incident, of which he writes that a swarm with greater capability but similar misalignment could within 6–12 months be "capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet." He also states that Anthropic's own recent alignment incidents were caused in part by "imperfect filtering of broken reinforcement learning environments." Sam Altman said publicly that OpenAI will adopt independent evaluators with employee-like access as well, and Musk voiced agreement — per CNBC, 14 September.
bullets.how: YES — the verification pattern being adopted by three frontier labs is the one PRAGMA already sells in miniature: an outside party with real access, publishing findings the subject cannot edit. When embedded, publish-rights evaluation becomes the industry norm at the top, "who audits your agents" becomes a procurement question at every layer below, and the AAIR registry is a scaled-down instance of exactly that shape. Second-order: pacing means capability steps arrive slower and more predictably, which favors building on a stable stack over chasing releases — and argues against any Construct plan whose value depends on a capability that has not shipped yet.

bullets.title: ANTHROPIC'S SEPTEMBER THREAT REPORT (10 SEP): THREAT ACTORS ARE NOW AUTHORING SKILLS, MALICIOUS INSTALLERS IMPERSONATE CLAUDE CODE, AND THE CLOSING ADVICE IS TO TREAT AI KEYS LIKE PRODUCTION CREDENTIALS
bullets.summary: "Detecting and countering misuse of AI: September 2026," covering activity disrupted December 2025 through August 2026. THE FINDING THAT LANDS ON OUR STACK: in GTG-20006 (Russian espionage, 20+ organizations) the human operator "engaged primarily to modify Claude Code skills that drove the workflows when they needed to be refined"; in GTG-10007 (Chinese-speaking, ~50 organizations) vendor firmware "was obtained and decrypted with a purpose-built skill"; and APPENDIX A IS A BREAKDOWN OF SKILLS DEVELOPED BY THREAT ACTORS. Separately, GTG-50021 ran a fraudulent reseller selling cheap "Claude access" that silently proxied to a different model while installing a credential harvester, with installers "spoofing as popular AI harnesses including Claude Code"; the harvester persisted and kept capturing new sessions on the device. GTG-50029, a single hacktivist, ran a month-long campaign against 42 European political targets "entirely on stolen API keys." The report's own framing of what changed: "None of the operations in this report depended on some entirely novel technique that defenders have never seen. Instead, the economics of the attacks have changed"; "sophistication has stopped being a reliable signal of who is behind an operation"; and the November 2025 autonomous operating model "has now proliferated across every class of actors we investigated." Closing advice quoted verbatim: "Organizations should treat AI keys and agent integrations with the same level of seriousness as they do production credentials—because attackers treat them with the same level of seriousness, too." SOURCE NOTE: the page was read via a subagent chunk-read and the capture TRUNCATED partway through the influence-operations section, so the scams-and-fraud, surveillance, biological, conventional-weapons and illicit-distillation sections were NOT read this fire.
bullets.how: YES, and it converts standing action (c) from housekeeping into triage. SKILL.md is The Construct's largest architectural commitment (~130 files, a dozen of them third-party) and it is now a DOCUMENTED ATTACK SURFACE IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: skills as the offensive tooling state actors refine by hand, and a spoofed-harness installer as the delivery vehicle. The provenance script — find + git log -1 across the third-party repos, plus the four Tenable greps including hidden Unicode — stops being tidy-up. And this is the THIRD independent source in four fires converging on the same unwritten item: Hermes holds one long-lived DreamHost deploy key plus GitHub write plus GSC, unrotated, unscoped and with no audience binding, which is exactly what the closing sentence is about. PRAGMA: "your agent integrations are production credentials" is now a quotable vendor line, not our opinion.

bullets.title: SAME REPORT, GTG-54002: A FRANCE-BASED AD AGENCY RAN ~70 FABRICATED NEWS SITES PUBLISHING 8,913 AI-WRITTEN ARTICLES IN ~20 LANGUAGES, ENGINEERED TO BOOST SEARCH-AUTHORITY RANKINGS
bullets.summary: Influence-as-a-service traced to LKM Company, a France-based digital advertising agency: roughly 70 fabricated news websites each paired with an X account, 250+ inauthentic commenting accounts created June–July 2025, and 8,913 articles in about 20 languages (318 of them DRC-focused). The articles were, in the report's words, "specifically designed to boost their site's authority rankings on search engines," under a house rule mandating 3–4 internal links per piece; multiple sites published near-identical DRC–Rwanda stories within three minutes of each other on 11 September 2025. Rated Category Two on the Breakout Scale. The report notes a broader shift in this class of operation: "Increasingly, operations are not run using individual prompts. Instead, a great deal is embedded within persistent memory files."
bullets.how: YES — this is the ADVERSARIAL TWIN of the B9 answer-page factory, and reading it as a specification of what not to do is the cheapest compliance check available. The factory rule that keeps us clear is already written (one page per real, provable subject; documented relationships only; never town-swapped or self-ranking variants), but the distinguishing feature in the wild is FABRICATED SUBJECT MATTER plus TEMPLATED INTERNAL-LINK ENGINEERING AT VOLUME, which justifies one explicit pass over the current B9 page set against those two markers specifically. It is also a sellable PRAGMA frame: AI-generated site networks built for authority laundering are now a named, documented category with a vendor citation, which raises the market value of provable provenance on the legitimate side. Note the persistent-memory line too — it is the same migration bullet 1 of 13 Sep found in the harness literature, observed here in the wild.

bullets.title: NOTHING SHIPPED — THIRD STRAIGHT DAY; CLAUDE CODE'S NEWEST CHANGELOG ENTRY IS STILL 2.1.270 (12 SEP, ONE LINE), THE DESKTOP CHANGELOG WAS NOT REACHABLE THIS FIRE AND NO CLAIM IS MADE ABOUT IT, AND THE ARXIV SLOT WAS LEFT EMPTY RATHER THAN PADDED
bullets.summary: Claude Code changelog read end-to-end at the primary: newest entry 2.1.270, dated 12 September 2026, containing exactly one line — "Fixed read-only git commands in Bash unexpectedly asking for permission after a session had been running for a while (regression in 2.1.269)." Nothing dated 13 or 14 September. The substantive release remains 2.1.269 (11 September). HONEST GAP: the Claude Desktop / Cowork changelog was NOT re-read this fire — it was not reachable from this session's fetch provenance — so nothing is asserted about it either way; last known state is v1.52386.3 (11 Sep) from the 13 Sep fire. KILL LIST, dates checked: the Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber / GPT-6 Astra / Fable-and-Mythos-5.1 cluster (1–3 Sep, already covered), NVIDIA/Perplexity investment TALKS at a $30B+ valuation (late-August URLs, still not a closed round), Perplexity's Agent API (13 Aug). ONE REAL DEADLINE SURVIVED THE SWEEP: Perplexity retires its Sonar endpoints on 27 SEPTEMBER 2026, which breaks any script still calling them. ARXIV: the sweep for new agent-skills, context-engineering and evaluation work returned only 2605–2608 papers already in or adjacent to scope (SkillsInjector, SkillAxe, ContinualSkillBench, Less Context Better Agents); nothing from this week's listing cleared the bar, AND NO BULLET WAS MANUFACTURED TO FILL THE SLOT.
bullets.how: MAYBE — a quiet vendor week is one line, not a bullet, and the only actionable item in the kill zone is the 27 September Sonar retirement, which is worth a single grep across our scripts for anyone who wired Perplexity in. The methodological note is the real content: this is the second consecutive fire in which ZERO useful items came from an aggregator, and the first in which an entire assigned category (arXiv) was reported EMPTY rather than backfilled with a three-month-old paper wearing this week's clothes. Also worth stating plainly rather than hiding: the Desktop changelog went unread, and 'not read' is being reported as not read.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — DAY FOURTEEN: THE LIST STAYS SORTED BY KIND, (c) CHANGES CATEGORY FROM HOUSEKEEPING TO ATTACK SURFACE, AND (b) REACHES ITS SEVENTH ASKING WITH FIVE LINES STILL UNWRITTEN
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's open decisions. CONFIG (write it into a settings file, where a machine enforces it): maxEffortLevel; --system-prompt-snapshot off; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS, still default and best left low until the incident log exists; coworkSessionRetentionDays CONFIRM UNSET, load-bearing because a retrospective trace audit is worth exactly as much as the traces that still exist; and (b) THE FOUR ENTRA MCP CONTROLS — SEVENTH ASKING, five lines, unwritten. ARTIFACT: (a) THE INCIDENT LOG — rows = AgentAudit's ten lifecycle dimensions (arXiv 2609.09875), security column = the eight requirements from arXiv 2609.00267, and as of today a THIRD independent source (bullet 2) saying the same thing about credentials; input = session transcripts already on disk; first entries already known — the four DCR-failed connectors (Asana, BigQuery, Box, HubSpot) and the two vendor-side permission-boundary near-misses fixed in 2.1.269. (c) SKILL-CORPUS AUDIT — RECATEGORISED BY BULLET 2 from maintenance to triage: find + git log -1 across the twelve third-party repos, plus the four Tenable greps including HIDDEN UNICODE; /skill-doctor still one unrun command. READ: RFC 9449 (DPoP), RFC 8707 (audience binding), and the body of arXiv 2609.00006. CARRIED: OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash on the credentialed executor; which dsh and ls ~/.dsh, unrun since 13 Sep. CLOSED 13 SEP: (e) cadence-cost measurement, closed unmeasured. NEW: Perplexity Sonar retires 27 Sep; and the Cowork-to-cloud / launchd seam is still unchecked.
bullets.how: YES. Completion count across fourteen days remains ZERO, and the honest read today is not another scolding but a RECLASSIFICATION: (c) was a documentation gap yesterday and is a named attack surface this morning, because the vendor's own threat report documents state actors refining Claude Code skills by hand and criminals shipping credential harvesters disguised as Claude Code installers. An unverified third-party skill corpus is no longer untidy. The same report supplies the one-sentence justification for (b) and (f) that thirteen fires of argument did not: treat AI keys and agent integrations with the same seriousness as production credentials. And bullet 1 supplies the structural lesson the list has been missing — the frontier labs did not fix their own verification problem with better intentions, they fixed it by giving an outside party access and publish rights the subject cannot edit. Put the check where the checked party does not control it.

praxis_lesson: THE FIELD SPENT TODAY AGREEING THAT AGENTS NEED AN OUTSIDE PARTY WITH REAL ACCESS AND PUBLISH RIGHTS — WHICH IS THE EXACT THING OUR OWN STACK STILL DOES NOT HAVE. Three frontier labs converged inside forty-eight hours on embedded evaluators, and the mechanism they chose is not better intentions but A SECOND PARTY WHO CAN SEE THE NUTS AND BOLTS AND CANNOT BE EDITED — desks, badges, laptops, internal-risk-team permissions, and a contract that forbids redacting a finding for being unfavourable. That is the same structural move as a config file versus a prose rule, and as a gate versus a good habit: PUT THE CHECK SOMEWHERE THE CHECKED PARTY DOES NOT CONTROL. Fourteen days of standing actions with zero completions is what the other arrangement produces. Meanwhile the threat report supplies the uncomfortable half of the same day: the workflows that hit ministries, hospitals, drone manufacturers and political parties this year were driven by SKILLS — one state operator "engaged primarily to modify Claude Code skills that drove the workflows" — an entire appendix catalogues skills built by threat actors, and criminals shipped credential harvesters "spoofing as popular AI harnesses including Claude Code." Our ~130-file skill corpus, a dozen of them third-party, has never had its provenance verified, and that item has been carried for a week under the heading of maintenance. IT IS NOT MAINTENANCE. The correct reading of a day where the vendor tells you to treat AI keys like production credentials, while your executor holds one unrotated, unscoped deploy key, is that the backlog just got re-priced by someone else. SECOND LESSON, ON SOURCING: the entire useful yield today came from two Anthropic primaries and one CEO's personal site — ZERO from aggregators, for the second consecutive fire — and the assigned arXiv category was reported EMPTY rather than filled with a three-month-old paper dressed in this morning's clothes. An empty category is a finding; a padded one is a lie with a citation. The same discipline applied to our own reading: the Desktop changelog was not reachable this fire and is reported as NOT READ rather than assumed unchanged, and the threat-report capture truncated before the scams-and-fraud section, which is stated in the bullet instead of quietly summarised over.
